title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: which transfer sets the reactivation Date
content:
## Scope

This rule applies to a Savings & Money Market Accounts account up for reactivation after its owner has sent money out of it in the contact. It fixes which posting on the account gives the reactivation Date.

## Policy clause

1. The transfer the owner makes in the contact is the latest outgoing item on the account that went out as a telephone banking transfer, an online transfer or a mobile app transfer.
2. So the reactivation Date is the latest posting Date among the account's outgoing items on those three channels, which is the posting Date of that transfer.
3. That posting Date is always a business Day, as the posting Date of any outgoing item is.

## Basis

- **Authority.** The outgoing items, their channels, their posting Dates: all of them come from the savings account's transaction history, not from what the owner says.
- **Object correlation.** Only this account's outgoing items on the three channels count here. Other outgoing items, such as ATM cash or internal transfers, play no part.

## Example (hypothetical)

| Outgoing item | Channel | Posting Date | Latest on the three channels? |
|---|---|---|---|
| online transfer to checking | online transfer | 3 March | no |
| telephone transfer to checking, in the contact | telephone banking | 14 July | yes |
| ATM cash | ATM | 20 July | not one of the three channels |

The latest item on the three channels is the telephone transfer posting on 14 July, so the reactivation Date is 14 July. The ATM item of 20 July is not on one of the three channels, so it plays no part.

## Points to note

**Mistaken view:** "Use the latest outgoing item on any channel." **Correct basis:** only telephone banking, online or mobile app transfers out count here.

**Mistaken view:** "Use the Date the owner calls, whatever the posting shows." **Correct basis:** the reactivation Date is the posting Date of that transfer, as the account's history shows it.
